description:
Profile and optimize arbitrary-offset bit shifts and coding permutations whose production cost is material on the target host.

## Background

BitVec explicitly dispatches whole-word shifts; residual-bit shifts use ordinary Rust loops. Circulant rotations, puncturing and interleaving are distinct operations with different data layouts and consumers. The presence of AVX2 or BMI2 is not sufficient reason to add a hot path.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Pass the shared behavioral and external conformance suites for every affected implementation, preserve the declared numerical contract and deterministic seeded execution, and exercise scalar fallback plus relevant empty, unaligned, partial-batch, and 0/1/63/64/65 bit-boundary cases. Compile intrinsic-bearing designs with Rust 1.95 before implementation decomposition; verify the shipped code at that MSRV.

- [hard] REQ-02: Publish committed before/after and matching open-source comparison receipts, with machine-readable samples and a Markdown interpretation, under the issue's configured dev/bench_results directory. Record exact commands, source and comparator revisions, input identities and seeds, compiler flags, runtime-selected paths, and runtime-observed hardware provenance. Register external sources in the citation registry and link durable artifacts at their final paths.

- [hard] REQ-03: Measure optimized release/bench builds on the Ryzen 9 5900X under the existing exclusive benchmark lock on a verified quiet host. Finish builds before measurement, record affinity, clocks/governor and SMT state, and use bounded resumable runs with an append-only execution log opened and printed before the first run.

- [hard] REQ-04: Freeze workloads, sample/repetition budgets, warmup, confidence level, improvement and per-cell non-regression tolerances, material-gap threshold, and stopping rules in a versioned premeasurement protocol before optimization trials. Cover small inputs, crossover regions, cache-resident and streaming sizes, kernel-only costs, setup/conversion costs, and representative production consumers; record inapplicable cells explicitly.

- [hard] REQ-05: Adopt production candidates only when the predeclared confidence-bound improvement and non-regression rules pass on their intended dispatch domain. Preserve all negative and inconclusive outcomes; retain the established implementation where no candidate qualifies. Report ratios to the fastest compatible measured external arm, without pooling incompatible operations or concealing losing cells in an aggregate.

- [hard] REQ-06: Explain outcomes with committed assembly and profiler evidence for instruction mix, dependencies, spills, allocation, cache traffic, or bandwidth limits. Preserve architecture boundaries and canonical abstractions, keep unsafe code in isolated kernels, and publish a ranked explanation and tracked disposition for every material residual gap. A documented no-win result is acceptable; an unexplained skipped comparison is not.

- [hard] REQ-07: Produce separate workload profiles and a reviewed worker-sized decomposition for shifts, QC/circulant rotations, puncturing and interleaving. Name the actual production consumer and select implementation leaves only where the predeclared materiality rule is met; preserve measured no-win/not-material outcomes for the others.

- [hard] REQ-08: Validate proposed AVX2 lane-crossing and any BMI-based design on Rust 1.95 before decomposition. Use observed capabilities and canonical dispatch/tuning, never a vendor-name assumption about BMI2 cost.

- [hard] REQ-09: Preserve exact bit indexing, wrap-versus-zero-fill behavior, aliasing contracts, tail padding and standards-defined permutation order. Cover offsets 0/1/7/8/63/64/65, larger-than-length shifts where defined, vector-lane crossings and incomplete words.

- [hard] REQ-10: Benchmark operation-equivalent paths from pinned external coding implementations where available, plus the established scalar/vector compiler baselines. Record exact adapter/representation costs and explicitly identify unmatched operations; a field-multiplication benchmark is not a permutation comparison.

- [hard] REQ-11: Publish latency/throughput and whole-consumer results; introduce reusable primitives only in their owning library layers. For compound paths, measure each representation conversion and memory pass before adopting a candidate.

## Notes

AFF3CT is an initial coding comparator; the source survey selects the strongest applicable implementation and records unsupported operation mappings. Numeric or scheduling changes are not implicit in this story.
title: Optimize arbitrary-offset shifts and coding permutations
